chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about slaughtering (al-dhakāh), and he said: 'It is not slaughtered except with iron; the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade that [other than iron].'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الذَّكَاةِ: Ritual slaughter of an animal for food
key_terms.بِحَدِيدَةٍ: With iron (specifying the material of the knife)

ai.seo_question: What material is required for ritual slaughter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies that ritual slaughter requires an iron instrument, a ruling attributed to Imam Ali (AS), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the purity and durability of the cutting tool. While the broader Islamic legal tradition permits any sharp object, this narration highlights a specific imamic preference for iron, underscoring the practical and spiritual integrity of the slaughter process. It serves as a key text in discussions regarding the material validity of the knife in Shia fiqh.
